Live frame captured and visually inspected; no runtime fault. Real nested graphs unsupported in this build; visual uses nested Three groups only.

Retain startup failures: initial default sandbox profile mkdir EPERM, corrected scoped escalation succeeded; default CIM process read denied, scoped retry verified identity. First authored library source had missing closing create brace and was rejected; corrected source built successfully before library activation. First prism tuning write rejected runtime generation1 after user resolution change to generation2; reread confirmed same source and identity, guarded generation2 write applied. UI Save shortcut did not open save outside Source focus; File Save opened native dialog, set_value returned UIA cache error, subsequent state showed user closed dialog with scene still Untitled. A graph UI action then explicitly reported user input detected; stopped input and asked async coordination. Source bundle backed up by read; no scene-save claim made. LUX116 independent review found auto-upgrade wording missing and incorrect SHA handoff; worker is correcting under same ticket, problem LUX-P103.

User requested no desktop UI after native-input conflict. Root stopped all UI actions; complete working source and live state are preserved in visuals/creative-upgrade-20260914/working-source-and-state.json, plus actual preview.png. Scene remains running; no scene-file save claimed. Independent coordinator reviewed exact corrected source d6a233c21d7f79dee61e266d36e6c7fb23d514b1 and reported source PASS. Root installed start-lux from that reviewed source worktree and ran --check successfully: current true; missing, changed, unexpected all empty. Coordinator owns serial integration and correction of stale original LUX116 ticket spec; corrected spec payload is visuals/creative-upgrade-20260914/start-lux-spec.json. Source validator Python exists but PyYAML missing; no claim that quick_validate.py passed.

items.summary: LUX-150 acceptance was recorded before a public ComponentDefinition source-compatibility regression was surfaced.
items.expected: Existing SDK 0.4 source may continue to annotate a code component as ComponentDefinition and access or call definition.create without rewriting the source.
items.actual: Submitted df472683234847f426f594ccdd414889c2783c61 and landed 72bdcfa9f53c8335c59fa3435b3ff77648375602 redefine ComponentDefinition as CodeComponentDefinition | GraphComponentDefinition. The strict compiler rejects the previously valid unguarded .create access; the changed regression test added a kind guard and therefore did not prove unchanged-source compatibility. The independent acceptance had already moved LUX-150 to done revision 5 before this evidence arrived. Conductor 0.2.0-dev rejects a later ticket reject on a done ticket with INVALID_STATE: ticket must be in review; no reopen command is documented.
items.correction: Treat the revision-5 acceptance as superseded for release. Preserve ComponentDefinition<C,I,O> as the compatibility alias to CodeComponentDefinition<C,I,O>, add a separately named AnyComponentDefinition union for graph containers and defineComponent internals, restore the exact old unguarded .create compile/link regression, rerun combined checks, then create and validate a linked bug-fix ticket because the accepted ticket cannot be reopened through the installed CLI.
items.evidence: Reviewer context codex:/root/review_component_design:component-definition-compatibility-correction-20260916. Integration record: artifacts/feedback-01a0a7bb/component-audio-integration.md. Superseded acceptance event: LUX-150 revision 5, event 765ddd04-359c-4369-a5dd-504f02852fca. Failed correction command returned INVALID_STATE with message `ticket must be in review`. LUX-151 behavior remains independently reviewed, but the bundled release is held until the linked compatibility fix lands and is reviewed.

notes.body:
Resolved prospectively by LUX-168. The exact submitted fix `6d8d7bef7679881b49bc2217d846b9533589d974`, landed through `4514291224282ebadfdc5885cc3a7e619d75161d`, restores the old unguarded `ComponentDefinition.create` annotation and introduces `AnyComponentDefinition` for code-or-graph annotations. The unchanged legacy source compiles and links, modern graph/type regressions pass, and independent review found no blockers.

Preserve the historical LUX-150 acceptance and this correction record. LUX-168 is the explicit compatibility closure for the release hold recorded here; it does not rewrite the earlier acceptance event.

Scope clarification recorded after the LUX-168 acceptance: future component migration is authorized when it preserves saved values, stable instance and Library links, and source history, with external limits disclosed. This does not undo or narrow the accepted LUX-168 compatibility fix, and it does not require a migration in LUX-168.
